sam: ugh. where are the logs / crash dumps?

2026-03-18T15:05:12Z runtime INFO: seq_len=8192 model=llama-13b kernel=quant-select commit=b3f9c2e

deploy-bot: Canary deploy SDG-23 started by nora (canary-2026-03-18T14:58) status: 3/5 unhealthy :warning:

jun: I pulled pmap/proc stats from one of the failing nodes. fragmentation and heap jump immediately after the commit rollout:
```text
before: heap used 8.1G, slab fragments 622
after:  heap used 12.4G, slab fragments 3100\fragmentation pattern: many small free chunks between pinned pagelets (hot-slab boundary)
```

nora: CI also caught a perf regression — runtime-perf/kv-regression job 8732 shows p50 token latency 2.1s -> 3.5s and increased memory churn. https://ci.example/8732

sam: can we reproduce this deterministically? command to run locally?

jun: repro script that hits the same code path (long ctx + prefix cache):
```bash
# run on devbox with same model/quant config
./bench --model=llama-13b --seq=8192 --batch=1 --prefix-cache \
  --timeout=600 --log-allocs | tee kv_repro.log
# force the kernel routing to quant-select to mimic canary
./bench --force-kernel=quant-select ...
```

maya: bisect plan: narrow commits between a4d7f11..b3f9c2e (deploy window yesterday). If the kernel-router decision tree is to blame it's probably the routing heuristics change in b3f9c2e. Can someone run git-bisect and the repro?

alex: I'm starting a bisect run on a beefy workstation now. will share the first bad commit if it reproduces. If confirmed i'll open a revert PR.

jun: quick CPU/mem profiling shows eviction path now schedules full-page compaction at ~200ms intervals under this workload; the compaction itself is expensive and creates many transient small free chunks which the slab allocator isn't coalescing efficiently. Flamegraph: https://perf.example/flame/9087 (high % in kv_compact_full and kernel_router::select_quant_path)

nora: hold the rollout and disable the feature flag for canaries until we confirm root cause. @deploy-bot please flip selective-quant->off for SDG-23 canaries. :no_entry_sign:

deploy-bot: Rolling back selective-quant for canary group SDG-23. Feature flag selective-quant = false. Rollback initiated, will report status.

Next steps: 1) bisect to exact commit, 2) add a small CI regression test that reproduces slab fragmentation (longctx + quant routing), 3) investigate allocator coalescing heuristic and compaction trigger thresholds.
